headline: Reference documentation is corrected across the toolkit: a mistyped signed-attribute field name, and options and return fields the code accepts or returns that the reference had omitted.
summary: The pki.smime.sign reference named the additionalSignedAttributes field oid; the code reads type, so the correct form is [{ type, values }] (as pki.cms already documents for unsignedAttributes). Options and return fields the code accepts or returns are now documented where the reference had left them out: pki.cms.sign additionalSignedAttributes; pki.cms.verify top-level eContent and the per-signer signedAttributes / unsignedAttrs / digestAlgorithm / countersignatures; pki.cms.authenticate oaepHash / ukm; pki.tsp.sign additionalSignedAttributes / digestAlgorithm / pss and pki.tsp.verify policyName; pki.pkcs12 mac.password and the pki.pkcs12.open valid field; pki.hpke.setupS sharedSecret; pki.path.validate userConstrainedPolicySet; pki.ocsp.verify matched; pki.asn1.decode maxItems and the node contentStart / contentEnd fields; pki.est.simpleenroll auth; and the pki.webauthn.verifyAssertion expectedChallenge / expectedOrigin / expectedTopOrigin options, which the verb checks against clientDataJSON when supplied. pki.ocsp.buildErrorResponse returns a Buffer (the signature had shown Buffer | string), the pki.schema.all example lists csrattrs, and the pki.acme.client method list includes updateAccount and listOrders. Reference prose across the toolkit and the documentation site is reworded for consistency. The one observable code change is that pki.tsp.verify now includes policyName on a failure verdict, the resolved policy name it already returned on a valid verdict.

Fixed: pki.smime.sign documented additionalSignedAttributes as [{ oid, values }]; the code reads the type field, so a caller following the reference would pass an unrecognized field. The correct form is [{ type, values }].
pki.ocsp.buildErrorResponse is documented as returning a Buffer; the signature previously showed Buffer | string, but the verb has no PEM option and every path returns DER.
The pki.schema.all example output lists csrattrs, which the enumeration returns between cmp and ocsp-request.
The pki.acme.client method list documents updateAccount and listOrders, which the client returns.

pki.tsp.verify now includes policyName on a failure verdict; it already returned the resolved policy name on a valid verdict and the raw policy on both, so a refused token carries the same descriptive fields as a valid one.
Changed: Options and return fields the code accepts or returns are now documented across pki.cms, pki.tsp, pki.pkcs12, pki.hpke, pki.path, pki.ocsp, pki.asn1, pki.est, pki.acme, and pki.webauthn. In particular, pki.webauthn.verifyAssertion is documented as checking the challenge and origin when expectedChallenge / expectedOrigin / expectedTopOrigin are supplied with clientDataJSON.
Reference prose across the toolkit and the documentation site is reworded for consistency.
